name: Start Webserver Authcerts Architecture
description: Architecture for the make start-webserver-authcerts target, covering the HTTPS nginx, oauth2-proxy, and Keycloak stack, together with the generated certificates, realm import, direct-url-auth config, and CALM CLI config selection required for local bearer-token access.

nodes.name: Architect
nodes.description: A human architect or operator who starts the cert-based local stack, follows the generated HTTPS host, and requests repository assets through the authenticated nginx front end.

nodes.name: Public Host Detection Helper
nodes.description: The scripts/detect_public_host.py helper that resolves the local host name or IP exported as CALM_PUBLIC_HOST before certificates, realm files, and the auth stack are generated and started.

nodes.name: Active CALM CLI Config Link
nodes.description: The ~/.calm.json symlink that the startup target rewires so local CALM CLI calls use the cert-based auth configuration.

nodes.name: Authcerts CALM CLI Config
nodes.description: The ~/.calmauthcerts.json configuration file selected for local HTTPS serving and direct URL authentication against the self-signed local stack.

nodes.name: Local TLS Certificate Assets
nodes.description: The generated certificate and private key under infra/nginx/certs, used by nginx for TLS termination and by oauth2-proxy as the trusted CA file for the local issuer.

nodes.name: Generated Keycloak Realm Import
nodes.description: The rendered Keycloak realm import generated from infra/keycloak/calm-local-realm.template.json, provisioning the calm-local realm, OAuth clients, and local test credentials for the auth stack.

nodes.name: Generated Direct URL Auth Config
nodes.description: The generated custom-idp/v2/generated/direct-url-auth.json file that supplies the local machine-client auth configuration for CALM CLI direct URL loading against the authenticated HTTPS origin.

nodes.name: Authcerts Static Content Tree
nodes.description: The static_authcerts content tree mounted directly into nginx so repository architectures, patterns, standards, controls, and related documentation are served through the authenticated HTTPS stack.

nodes.name: Nginx Static Web Server
nodes.description: The nginx Compose service started by make start-webserver-authcerts, serving repository assets over authenticated HTTPS on port 8443, exposing oauth2-proxy under /oauth2/, and reverse proxying Keycloak under /keycloak/.

nodes.name: OAuth2 Proxy
nodes.description: The oauth2-proxy container that enforces bearer-token or OIDC-backed access for protected static content and exchanges identity data with Keycloak for the local auth flow.

nodes.name: Keycloak Identity Provider
nodes.description: The Keycloak container that runs the calm-local realm, serves OIDC metadata and token endpoints, and backs the local admin console exposed through nginx.

relationships.description: Architects run the public host detection helper to discover which local host will be embedded into the generated auth-aware assets and HTTPS endpoint.
The detected CALM_PUBLIC_HOST value informs the nginx startup flow and the HTTPS host presented to local clients.
The detected host is injected into the generated Keycloak realm import so local issuer and redirect settings match the HTTPS origin.
The detected host is written into the generated direct URL auth configuration so CALM CLI machine-client requests target the correct local HTTPS origin.
The startup target rewires ~/.calm.json so the active CALM CLI config points at ~/.calmauthcerts.json before the authenticated HTTPS stack is started.
The selected CALM CLI config references the generated direct URL auth configuration so local machine-client validation can authenticate to the protected HTTPS origin.
The nginx server serves static repository assets from the mounted static_authcerts content tree.
Nginx terminates HTTPS with the generated local certificate and private key mounted from infra/nginx/certs.
Oauth2-proxy trusts the generated local CA certificate so it can validate the public Keycloak issuer exposed through nginx.
Nginx routes authentication callbacks and auth checks under /oauth2/ to oauth2-proxy so protected static content requires a valid bearer token or OIDC session.
Oauth2-proxy validates JWTs, redeems tokens, and reads OIDC metadata against the calm-local Keycloak realm during the local authentication flow.
Nginx exposes Keycloak's admin console and OIDC endpoints under /keycloak/ so the local HTTPS origin fronts both static content and identity flows.
Keycloak loads the generated calm-local realm import at startup so the local OAuth clients, service account, and test credentials are available.
Architects request repository content from nginx over authenticated HTTPS on port 8443 while the anonymous /healthz endpoint remains available for operational checks.
